history.dynasty: Pandyas (rock-cut shrine); renovations by the Madurai Nayaks (1736)
history.period: 6th-8th century CE (rock-cut Pandya work); mentioned in Sangam literature; exact construction date disputed — sources variously say 6th century AD / 8th-century Pandya (verify)
history.summary: CSV CORRECTIONS: spelling corrected from 'Thirupparamkunram' to Thiruparankundram; town corrected from 'Madurai' — the temple stands at Thiruparankundram town, about 8 km southwest of Madurai city. This is the FIRST of the six Arupadai Veedu (abodes) of Lord Murugan and among the oldest rock-cut temples in Tamil Nadu: the sanctum is carved directly into the Parankundram hill. Legend holds that Murugan married Deivanai, daughter of Indra, here after his victory over the demon Surapadman — hence Murugan is worshipped in wedding form, and the temple is considered auspicious for marriages. The hill and temple are mentioned in ancient Tamil Sangam works including Silappathikaram and Tirumurugatrupadai. Dravidian rock-cut architecture: sculptures carved on the rock wall, a 7-tiered ~150-ft Rajagopuram, and the Kambathadi, Ardha and Maha mandapams at different levels; free and special (Rs.100) darshan queues; sanctum reached by ~50 steep steps. Five theerthams in and around the temple (Saravana Poigai, Lakshmi Theertham, Saniyasi Koneru, Kasi Sunai, Sathiya Koopam). ~25-32 km by road from the sixth abode, Pazhamudircholai (seq 940).

name: Thirupparamkunram Murugan Temple
town: Thiruparankundram (CSV town 'Madurai' is approximate — ~8 km southwest of Madurai city)
town_description: Thiruparankundram is a town about 8 km southwest of Madurai city in Madurai district, Tamil Nadu, named for the Parankundram hill whose rock-cut Murugan shrine is the first of the six Arupadai Veedu; it has its own railway station and is well connected to Madurai.

travel.railway: Thiruparankundram railway station (local) and Madurai Junction — about 8 km (verify).
travel.road: Regular buses, taxis and private vehicles connect the temple with Madurai and nearby cities.

visitor_information.best_time: November to April for pleasant weather; Skanda Sashti and Panguni Uthiram are the grandest (and most crowded) festival seasons.
